T01 [00:00] Agent: Hello, is that Ryan Fletcher? I'm calling from vehicle finance collections.
T02 [00:05] Customer: Yeah, what's this about?

T04 [00:14] Customer: Ryan Fletcher, thirtieth of May nineteen ninety-five, NE6 2BX.
T05 [00:21] Agent: And the first line of your address?
T06 [00:24] Customer: 18 Corbridge Street.
T07 [00:27] Agent: Thank you, that's all verified. There are now three missed instalments on your account and the arrears are increasing.
T08 [00:37] Customer: I know. I've had a lot on. My car insurance went up by ninety pounds a month at renewal and I've been juggling things.
T09 [00:48] Agent: I understand. To find an affordable arrangement, I'd like to go through your income and expenditure with you. Can we do that now?
T10 [00:58] Customer: No. I'm not going through all my finances on the phone. My money's fine, I just need to catch up.

T14 [01:29] Customer: Right. I get it.
T15 [01:32] Agent: Can you tell me what that means for you?
T16 [01:35] Customer: If I don't sort it, you could take further steps, maybe take the car.
T17 [01:42] Agent: That's right. When on Friday could we speak to agree an amount?

summary: DPA completed. The company called and reached the customer, and arrears were discussed. A car insurance increase of £90 a month at renewal has left the customer juggling payments. The customer declined an I&E assessment, stating their finances were fine, and the agent attempted to secure a payment, but the customer declined; the agent warned that the account is at risk of further action, including a default notice and vehicle recovery, and checked the customer's understanding. The next steps are for the company to call on 13 November after 5 pm to agree a payment amount.

transcript:
T01 [00:00] Agent: Good morning, vehicle finance, how can I help?
T02 [00:04] Customer: Hi, I got a letter saying I'm behind. I want to pay what I can.
T03 [00:10] Agent: Of course. Can I have your full name, date of birth, first line of your address and postcode?
T04 [00:17] Customer: Hannah Price, fourth of April nineteen ninety. 26 Willow Bank, Norwich, NR3 1TA.
T05 [00:26] Agent: Thank you, that's all confirmed. There's one missed instalment showing. What happened with that one?
T06 [00:34] Customer: My hours were cut at the care home in October, so I was about a hundred and twenty pounds short that month.
T07 [00:44] Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to make a payment by card now?
T08 [00:49] Customer: Yes, I can do seventy-five pounds today.
T09 [00:54] Agent: I'll take you through to secure payment. Thank you for waiting. I'm afraid the card was declined by your bank.
T10 [01:28] Customer: Oh no. I think I'm over my daily limit after paying rent this morning.
T11 [01:35] Agent: That can happen. Would you like to try again another day?
T12 [01:40] Customer: Can I pay the seventy-five on the nineteenth through the portal? I'll definitely have it then.
T13 [01:48] Agent: Yes. So that's seventy-five pounds through the online portal on Thursday the nineteenth of November. Is that affordable?
T14 [01:58] Customer: Yes, it is.
T15 [02:01] Agent: Just to check you're clear, can you repeat the plan back to me?
T16 [02:06] Customer: Seventy-five pounds on the portal on the nineteenth, and I'll ring my bank about the limit.
T17 [02:14] Agent: Perfect. We'll check the payment has arrived on the twentieth of November and contact you if it hasn't.
T18 [02:24] Customer: Thanks.
summary: DPA completed. The customer called the company and arrears were discussed. Reduced hours in October left the customer about £120 short that month. The agent attempted to take a card payment, but it was declined by the customer's bank, which the customer believed was due to a daily limit; the agent checked the customer's understanding, and the customer agreed to pay £75 through the online portal on 19 November. The next steps are for the customer to contact their bank about the limit and for the company to check receipt of the payment on 20 November.

transcript:
T01 [00:00] Agent: Hello, could I speak to Kwame Asante, please? I'm calling from vehicle finance collections.
T02 [00:05] Customer: Speaking.
T03 [00:07] Agent: Before we continue, please confirm your full name, date of birth, first line of your address and postcode.
T04 [00:14] Customer: Kwame Asante, eleventh of November nineteen seventy-five. 64 Mill Lane, Bolton, BL1 4SJ.
T05 [00:23] Agent: Thank you, security is complete. I'm calling about the missed instalment this month. Is everything all right?
T06 [00:31] Customer: Not really. I was made redundant three weeks ago. I've applied for Universal Credit but the first payment won't come for another five weeks.
T07 [00:44] Agent: I'm very sorry. That's a difficult situation. Do you have any income at the moment?
T08 [00:50] Customer: Only my redundancy pay, and most of that went on rent arrears. I've got about forty pounds to last me until the end of the month.
T09 [01:03] Agent: Thank you for explaining. Would you be happy for me to record that you've been made redundant and are waiting for Universal Credit, so we can take it into account?
T10 [01:15] Customer: Yes, that's fine.
T11 [01:18] Agent: Thank you, I've noted that with your consent. Citizens Advice can give you free help with your benefits claim and your debts. Would you like their details?
T12 [01:30] Customer: Yes please, I didn't know where to start.
T13 [01:34] Agent: I'll text you their details after the call. I'm also putting a thirty-day hold on collection contact while you get advice.
T14 [01:44] Customer: Thank you. Does that mean I don't owe anything for now?
T15 [01:49] Agent: No, the arrears stay on the account, but we won't chase you during the hold. Is that clear?
T16 [01:57] Customer: Yes, it's paused, not cancelled.
T17 [02:01] Agent: Exactly. We'll call you on the fourteenth of December to see where things are with Universal Credit.
T18 [02:10] Customer: Okay. Thanks for being decent about it.
summary: DPA completed. The company called and reached the customer, and arrears were discussed. The customer was made redundant three weeks ago and is waiting five weeks for a first Universal Credit payment; redundancy pay went on rent arrears, leaving about £40 until the end of the month; Consent gained to record vulnerability. The customer was referred to National Debtline, and the agent checked understanding that the hold does not cancel the arrears. A thirty-day hold on collection contact was applied, and the next steps are to seek advice before the company calls on 14 December.

The customer's working hours were reduced and they have entered a debt management plan. The agent accepted a temporary arrangement of £45 a month by standing order starting on 1 January, to be reviewed in six months. The next steps are for the company to send written confirmation to the customer and the debt management company within five working days.
